1	# Family delivery manifest contract, version 1
2	
3	This is the local file contract for registry 2.2.0 family candidates in [PIXL/2](PIXL-2.md). It does not describe a remote service or an artistic judgment. Existing PX1/PX2 documents without the explicit family fields retain their prior interpretation.
4	
5	## Canonical shape
6	
7	The manifest is UTF-8 JSON with sorted keys, compact separators, unescaped Unicode and one final LF. Duplicate keys/noncanonical serialization are rejected through exact canonical byte comparison. Maximum encoded size is 16 MiB, JSON nesting 64, all numbers finite. Its SHA-256 is both the X.dg and containing directory name. Exact top-level keys:
8	
9	| Field | Meaning |
10	| --- | --- |
11	| version | Integer 1 |
12	| output, candidate | Owning family F ID and this manifest X ID |
13	| source_state_sha256 | Canonical digest of the immediately preceding saved state |
14	| created_at | ISO timestamp with explicit UTC offset, at most six fractional digits |
15	| plan | Frozen planning identity and semantic bindings described below |
16	| baseline | Exact `candidate` ID and canonical `record_sha256` of the baseline X |
17	| files | Ordered frozen member entries described below |
18	| acceptance | Exactly `accepted: false` and `source_status`, the pre-snapshot family report |
19	| limits | Exactly `retention_only: true`, `remote_executed: false`, `automatic_acceptance: false` |
20	
21	Plan has exactly output, task, baseline, members, destinations and bindings. The first three are record IDs. Members is the saved distinct ordered F list, destinations the saved distinct I list, and bindings maps each ID in the full semantic scope of the family F to its canonical record SHA-256. P/T/E/V/J/N are excluded under existing proof rules. The map includes baseline X, member F plans, destinations and their semantic dependencies. Current task states and actual V/E outcomes remain in source_status and the preceding state history, not in that hash closure.
22	
23	Each files entry has exactly output, candidate, source_path, path, sha256, bytes and record_sha256. Output is the corresponding saved member F; candidate is its exact selected X. source_path is that X's project-relative path. path is `files/0000<suffix>` (zero-based member index, four digits). The original final suffix is retained when it matches a dot followed by 1–16 ASCII alphanumeric characters; otherwise use `.bin`. sha256 and bytes identify the exact copied bytes; record_sha256 binds the source X's full canonical fields. Maximum 1024 members, 256 MiB each, 512 MiB in total.
24	
25	The family X is report kind with of=output and xs=[baseline, each files candidate in order]. It has no raster contract. The baseline may also occur in files. Candidate/record references are typed in X.xs and are checked against the manifest; JSON IDs alone do not supply graph context.
26	
27	## Files and publication
28	
29	The store is a proper subdirectory of the explicit project root. A snapshot resides at `STORE/deliveries/<manifest-sha256>/manifest.json`, with the numbered member files in its `files/` directory. Source files are not moved or rewritten. All resolved paths remain in their declared directories; redirected manifest/member locations and different existing immutable bytes fail. Every rooted validation checks actual retained copies and source identities.
30	
31	Publication requires an existing saved PX2 family plan. The new manifest must exactly describe the immediately preceding canonical state, its current accepted baseline/member selection and report; its plan must remain unchanged in the candidate state. Both prior and candidate state must satisfy snapshot readiness. Generic commit enforces these requirements and store paths, just as the snapshot helper does. An initialized store cannot invent prior snapshot history. An existing X cannot acquire xs retroactively.
32	
33	The snapshot helper and generic snapshot publication add only one new X, with existing records unchanged. No E/V, task state, nomination, approval or provider event is created. Retain the candidate first, then inspect and record the result separately; other intentional edits use another revision. All mutations use expected-hash compare-and-swap. Stale/failed publication never publishes a candidate; unreferenced immutable files may remain and are not an accepted delivery. state.px is the publication authority.
34	
35	Published manifest X and every X named by its xs are immutable. A revision adds new X IDs, preserving original source and copied bytes. Existing family plans cannot shed bs/mb/ds, and old manifest candidates cannot shed xs. Intentional membership/destination/criteria changes are explicit plan revisions, with completed-task reopening and E/V supersession where applicable.
36	
37	## Historical existence versus current acceptance
38	
39	Old packages are checked against their saved members and typed constituents, so changing current F.mb does not erase or make old packages structurally invalid. Reports compare saved semantic bindings and selection to the current plan and report drift. A current pass/fail family V requires both current selection and saved semantic planning identity to match its candidate. Otherwise supersede that verdict, preserve the old candidate and reopen affected work. An unavailable V remains a retained account of why inspection was not performed.
40	
41	Family reports require a project root and include pending jobs for baseline/member/delivery tasks. Unrooted graph validation can check typed structure and current selection, but cannot read frozen manifest bindings or copied bytes; it does not establish current package validity. Store publication and family reports require rooted checks. Pending prepared/submitted/running/unknown work prevents a fresh snapshot and is routed through the provider recovery skill. A family that lacks confirmed destination or applicable adoption may still retain useful local accepted-member bytes; it cannot use that retention to activate or complete delivery. Continuity inspection, engine execution and human artistic approval remain actual obligations supplied by the task's declared Q and real observations.
42	
43	## Visible asset lineage
44	
45	Rooted `family` reports derive `lineage` beside each currently selected member and
46	beside each historical snapshot file. `review-context` exposes the same projection
47	for its candidate and delivered members. PLAR delivery status carries nominated
48	candidate lineage and the nominated family snapshot's members into fresh handoffs.
49	When PLAR links the family output itself to a directory, delivery observation checks
50	every distinct manifest `source_path` beneath that directory against its retained
51	member size and SHA-256. It does not infer destination names, count unrelated files
52	as members, or treat the manifest digest as a directory digest. The nominated
53	snapshot must still match the current accepted family, its selections and pending
54	work; these read-time file checks create no acceptance or new saved-state fields.
55	These are read-time views of existing artifact and durable-job identities, not new
56	PX2 fields or changes to the immutable manifest contract above. Historical reports
57	and handoffs keep their original bytes; read current state for a fresh projection.
58	
59	A retained import binds an exact candidate record to its journal event. The saved
60	request and caller-supplied observations describe what was requested or reported;
61	local hash and history validation does not authenticate remote execution. A tool
62	name, success state, provider ID, style baseline, task input or equal file hash alone
63	does not establish pixel ancestry. Family `X.xs` remains a constituent list. Where
64	an exact relationship is absent, ambiguous or unavailable, lineage must preserve
65	that limit rather than invent an origin. Equal bytes can support byte-equivalence
66	without establishing which copy was the source.
67	
68	The derived view identifies its `candidate` and `sha256`. `artifact.jobs` names
69	its direct importing jobs; `jobs` contains bounded supporting job details and their
70	recorded `source_requests`. `same_bytes` lists equivalences; `workflow_inputs`
71	retains task context. `provenance_status` distinguishes a retained import, equality
72	to recorded imported bytes, and an unrecorded origin;
73	`remote_verified` stays false. Request operation labels describe saved intent,
74	not successful artistic outcomes. Explicit simulation evidence remains visible.
75	Nested source requests are bounded and unresolved references retain their locator.
76	The exact retained journal is the source for omitted details. Workflow inputs and
77	equal-byte candidates are context, not inferred directed ancestry.
78	
79	Lineage is independent of acceptance. It creates no job, artifact, review, verdict,
80	nomination or completion. Derived relationships do not convert a controlled fixture
81	into real generation or a deterministic correction into a successful generative
82	animation. Larger caller results use the existing exact delivery/resume locators;
83	they must not silently omit lineage to fit the inline budget.
84

1	# Selected asset to first candidate request
2	
3	`plar prepare --root ROOT --asset ID --requirements HASH --packet PACKET_JSON --connection CONNECTION_JSON [--store STORE] [--path plar.txt] [--revise --expect STATE_HASH]`
4	and `pixl_plar_prepare` prepare the first candidate for a selected PLAR asset.
5	The normal output is an existing PX2 sample plan plus its first durable provider job.
6	The operation executes locally and returns the normal job state/next action. It

1	# Destination observation import (NF-06)
2	
3	This read-state operation validates a supplied destination report against an exact,
4	current family candidate and writes a fresh retained evidence export. It never runs
5	the renderer, changes `.px` state, creates E/V records, nominates a candidate, or
6	accepts art. A caller must actually inspect the returned PNG previews and make an
7	explicit [candidate review](candidate-review.md) when that work is justified.
8	
9	The operation adds no UDL fields or migration. The existing
10	[PIXL-2](PIXL-2.md), `pixl/registry-v2.json`, and
11	[family-delivery](family-delivery.md) semantics remain authoritative. In particular,
12	a valid historical manifest is insufficient: its member selection and frozen plan
13	must still be current.
14	
15	## Operation
16	
17	Python:
18	
19	```python
20	import_observation(doc, root, candidate_id, report_path, out)
21	```
22	
23	`doc` is the already loaded state document; `root` is the declared consumer root.
24	`report_path` and `out` are canonical forward-slash relative paths beneath that root.
25	`out` must not exist. Absolute, parent-traversal, backslash, drive-prefixed and
26	redirected symlink paths are rejected. Inputs must be regular files. Source and
27	destination paths are declarations to validate and retain, never executable commands.
28	
29	Public adapters expose `destination-import` and `pixl_destination_import`; the
30	service operation takes `path`, `candidate_id`, `report_path`, and `out`. The tool
31	reads state and writes evidence. Its state is unchanged, but its filesystem effects
32	must not be described as read-only.
33	
34	```text
35	destination-import STATE CANDIDATE REPORT_JSON --out FRESH_DIR --root ROOT
36	```
37	
38	As with ordinary CLI state commands, `STATE` resolves from the working directory
39	and must stay inside `ROOT`. `REPORT_JSON`, `FRESH_DIR`, and optional
40	`--result-path` resolve beneath `ROOT`. The MCP state `path` is consumer-relative.
41	The example queue runner's `renderer/observation.py --help` describes its optional
42	capture-to-report adapter, including the explicit member-output destination map.
43	
44	## Version 1 report
45	
46	The executable closed schema is `REPORT_SCHEMA` in
47	`pixl/destination_observation.py`. Every object rejects additional fields; every
48	listed field is required. Hashes are lowercase SHA-256. IDs and ordinary text are
49	nonblank strings. JSON duplicate keys, booleans used as numbers, nonfinite numbers,
50	and fractional JSON numbers used as integers are rejected.
51	
52	| Field | Shape and meaning |
53	| --- | --- |
54	| `version` | Integer `1`. |
55	| `candidate` | Exact family X ID passed to the operation. |
56	| `binding_hash` | Current `review-context` semantic binding hash for that candidate. A state hash is not a substitute. |
57	| `manifest` | `{path, sha256}` exactly matching `review-context.candidate_file`. The actual canonical family manifest is verified and retained. |
58	| `observed_at` | ISO timestamp with an explicit timezone offset, no later than import time. This is supplied metadata, not an independently established capture time. |
59	| `renderer` | `{name, command, runtime, files}`. `command` is a nonempty argv string array; `runtime` is `{name, version}`; `files` is a nonempty array of `{path, sha256}` source identities. |
60	| `consumer_sources` | Nonempty array of `{path, sha256}` for declared consumer sources. |
61	| `destinations` | Exactly one `{output, candidate, path, sha256}` for each manifest member. `output`, `candidate`, and hash must identify that exact member. `path` names the actual supplied served copy to read and retain. |
62	| `viewport` | `{width, height, device_scale_factor}` with positive integer dimensions and positive finite scale factor. |
63	| `views` | Array of `{consumer, state, scale, output_id, member_outputs}`. `scale` is positive and finite. `output_id` references a declared PNG. `member_outputs` contains unique manifest output IDs; an empty list can describe a contextual view showing no member. |
64	| `motion` | Array of motion records described below. |
65	| `files` | Nonempty array of `{id, path, sha256, role}` with unique IDs and paths. `role` is `image`, `data`, or `log`; every `image` must verify as PNG. |
66	| `limitations` | Array of nonblank supplied limitations. Import does not replace or resolve them. |
67	
68	A motion record is:
69	
70	```json
71	{
72	  "consumer": "caller-defined consumer",
73	  "state": "caller-defined state",
74	  "mode": "caller-defined playback mode",
75	  "status": "observed",
76	  "frame_count": null,
77	  "frame_ms": null,
78	  "samples": [{"elapsed_ms": 0, "frame": null, "output_id": "view-0"}],
79	  "limitation": "Timing metadata was unavailable; sample bytes were supplied."
80	}
81	```
82	
83	`status` is `observed` or `unavailable`. Observed motion requires one or more
84	samples; unavailable motion requires an empty sample list. `frame_count` is a
85	positive integer or `null`; `frame_ms` is a positive finite number or `null`.
86	Each sample has a nonnegative finite `elapsed_ms`, a nonnegative integer `frame`
87	or `null`, and an image `output_id`. Elapsed times strictly increase within each
88	motion record. When both frame index and frame count are known, the index must be
89	less than the count. Null means unknown; zero is not substituted for unknown
90	timing. Unavailable observations remain distinct from observed samples whose
91	metadata is partly unknown.
92	
93	Consumer names, states, playback modes, view scales, frame timing and sample
94	counts remain caller-defined observations. The operation contains no `full` /
95	`compact`, 1x / 3x, looping, animation-quality, or artistic acceptance requirement.
96	Declared source completeness and provenance remain reviewer concerns: the importer
97	can verify declared bytes but cannot infer undeclared renderer dependencies.
98	
99	## Validation and retained export
100	
101	Before creating `out`, import validates the rooted state and exact family candidate,
102	current semantic binding, canonical manifest, all member destination hashes, every
103	declared source/output hash, and view/motion references. It snapshots all declared
104	bytes before export, rechecks them for changes, and revalidates state dependencies.
105	After writing the bundle and previews, it rechecks input bytes and state dependencies
106	again before writing the success receipt. This catches changes observed during the
107	operation; it does not lock the caller's working tree or attest execution history.
108	
109	The fresh output contains:
110	
111	- `<sha256>.zip`: a deterministic content-addressed archive with fixed generated
112	  internal paths. It retains the original report bytes as `report.json`, the actual
113	  canonical manifest as `package/manifest.json`, all declared renderer and consumer
114	  source bytes, all served destination copies, all declared output bytes, and
115	  `index.json`. The index maps original paths, hashes, sizes and output IDs to
116	  generated archive entries. ZIP timestamps, entry ordering and permissions are
117	  fixed; output directory names do not affect archive identity.
118	- `previews/NNNN.png`: exact copies of each declared image output, with measured
119	  dimensions and hashes returned for actual inspection.
120	- `result.json`: written last as the successful export receipt. A partially written
121	  directory is preserved on failure and cannot be reused by retry.
122	
123	The importer only writes its own archive. It does not extract or execute archives.
124	The raw report and original paths remain traceable within the ZIP, while all retained
125	bytes use generated internal names.
126	
127	The result includes state, candidate, binding, report and manifest identities;
128	declared renderer/consumer/destination/output identities; bundle and preview
129	references; supplied viewport/view/motion/limitation values; and explicit
130	`renderer_executed: false`, `state_changed: false`, and
131	`automatic_acceptance: false`. `files_verified: true` means declared byte identities
132	passed these checks, not that a renderer actually ran or art passed review.
133	
134	`observation` is a ready `{path, sha256, mode: "live", note}` reference to the ZIP for
135	an explicit candidate review. The mode describes the supplied destination evidence
136	category. It does not attest execution or create a passing verdict. A reviewer can
137	also attach the separately inspected PNG previews with the mode required by the
138	criterion. Existing candidate-review retention copies the complete ZIP, so report
139	inputs and outputs survive removal of their original files and of this intermediate
140	export. This is why a report JSON alone is insufficient retention evidence.
141	
142	## Resource bounds and failure behavior
143	
144	The report and manifest use the existing codec document-size cap. Each captured
145	file is at most 64 MiB; unique captured bytes and assembled archive input bytes are
146	each at most 256 MiB. The final ZIP must be at most 64 MiB, matching the existing
147	candidate-review per-file limit. PNGs that trigger Pillow decompression-bomb limits
148	are rejected. Size bounds are retention safeguards, not asset design rules.
149	
150	The closed schema additionally bounds text to 16,384 characters; argv to 256
151	entries; renderer files, consumer sources, destinations and motion records to 1,024
152	each; views to 4,096; files and samples per motion record to 16,384; viewport
153	dimensions and frame count to 65,536; scale factors to 64; and timing values to
154	10^12 milliseconds. The overall document and byte limits can be reached sooner.
155	
156	Malformed/changed input or stale bindings fail before output publication when
157	detected during preparation. An I/O failure or detected input change after writing
158	starts preserves the partial export and omits its success receipt. No existing
159	evidence is overwritten or removed. A caller retains the failure, corrects the
160	cause, obtains current review context where needed, and chooses a fresh `out`.
161	
162	These checks establish consistency and durable bytes. Runtime execution,
163	independent viewing, renderer provenance, useful artistic revision, and final target
164	acceptance need their own evidence; this import operation does not establish them.
165

1	# Reviewed task completion
2	
3	`task-complete STORE TASK CANDIDATE... --expect HASH --root ROOT` and
4	`pixl_task_complete({store,expect,task_id,candidates})` nominate explicit existing
5	candidates and complete their PX2 task. This is a local publication operation;
6	it creates no criteria, decisions, evidence, verdicts, asset files or provider calls.
7	It adds no UDL fields and preserves the existing registry/lifecycle semantics.
8	
9	Every planned output needs exactly one supplied candidate owned by that output.
10	Every saved required criterion must already have a current passing verdict for
11	that candidate. Missing, failed, unavailable or stale acceptance cannot complete.
12	All normal prerequisite, choice, adoption, baseline and file-binding checks apply.
13	Prepared/unknown/submitted/running jobs on this task must be reconciled first.
14	Dropped tasks and changes to already-completed selections require explicit reopening.
15	
16	The expected hash is checked under the store lock. The complete transition sequence
17	is validated before publication. An open or blocked task publishes the ordinary
18	active revision and then the done revision, retaining both snapshots; an active
19	task needs one revision. The operation holds the writer lock throughout. Validation
20	failure leaves state unchanged. Storage interruption between publications can leave
21	a valid active state; read workflow/current hash and resume without repeating any
22	provider request. Hard process termination may leave the existing store lock; follow the normal stale-lock owner check before recovery. This is not a multi-file all-or-nothing transaction.
23	
24	An already-done task with the same selection and expected hash returns
25	`already_complete:true` without another revision. Results include state/hash/revision,
26	selected candidate IDs, task ID, publication history and explicit
27	`acceptance_created:false` / `remote_executed:false`. Files still need the caller's
28	assigned destination integration and actual review; this operation only publishes
29	completion supported by the existing saved acceptance plan.
30	
31	PLAR-bound continuation uses the [allocation/revision contract](asset-preparation.md#allocation-and-revised-work). Pending attempts for the same explicitly tagged asset exclude new jobs even under different task/output IDs. New task activation/completion checks the current selection and selected generation; retained historical validation is unchanged.

# Reviewed task completion

`task-complete STORE TASK CANDIDATE... --expect HASH --root ROOT` and
`pixl_task_complete({store,expect,task_id,candidates})` nominate explicit existing
candidates and complete their PX2 task. This is a local publication operation;
it creates no criteria, decisions, evidence, verdicts, asset files or provider calls.
It adds no UDL fields and preserves the existing registry/lifecycle semantics.

Every planned output needs exactly one supplied candidate owned by that output.
Every saved required criterion must already have a current passing verdict for
that candidate. Missing, failed, unavailable or stale acceptance cannot complete.
All normal prerequisite, choice, adoption, baseline and file-binding checks apply.
Prepared/unknown/submitted/running jobs on this task must be reconciled first.
Dropped tasks and changes to already-completed selections require explicit reopening.

The expected hash is checked under the store lock. The complete transition sequence
is validated before publication. An open or blocked task publishes the ordinary
active revision and then the done revision, retaining both snapshots; an active
task needs one revision. The operation holds the writer lock throughout. Validation
failure leaves state unchanged. Storage interruption between publications can leave
a valid active state; read workflow/current hash and resume without repeating any
provider request. Hard process termination may leave the existing store lock; follow the normal stale-lock owner check before recovery. This is not a multi-file all-or-nothing transaction.

An already-done task with the same selection and expected hash returns
`already_complete:true` without another revision. Results include state/hash/revision,
selected candidate IDs, task ID, publication history and explicit
`acceptance_created:false` / `remote_executed:false`. Files still need the caller's
assigned destination integration and actual review; this operation only publishes
completion supported by the existing saved acceptance plan.

PLAR-bound continuation uses the [allocation/revision contract](asset-preparation.md#allocation-and-revised-work). Pending attempts for the same explicitly tagged asset exclude new jobs even under different task/output IDs. New task activation/completion checks the current selection and selected generation; retained historical validation is unchanged.

def selection_bindings(document, task_id, root, folder=None):
    """Report opt-in live PLAR selections carried by immutable task input reports."""
    result = []
    for reference in document.records[task_id].fields["ip"]:
        artifact = document.records[reference.id]
        metadata = artifact.fields.get("mt", {})
        if metadata.get("binding") != "pixl.plar.selection/1":
            continue
        row = {"input": artifact.id, "snapshot": artifact.fields["ur"], **metadata}
        try:
            if artifact.fields["kd"].value != "report" or not all(
                isinstance(metadata.get(k), str)
                for k in ("plar_path", "asset_id", "requirements_hash")
            ):
                raise PixlError("plar_binding", "invalid version-1 selection metadata")
            current = read(root, metadata["plar_path"], metadata["asset_id"], include_production=False)
            row["current_requirements_hash"] = current["requirements_hash"]
            link = current["asset"].get("production")
            row["selected_for_asset"] = link is None or (link["task"] == task_id and (folder is None or graph.confined(root, link["store"]) == Path(folder).resolve()))
            row["linked_task"] = link["task"] if link else None
            row["linked_store"] = link["store"] if link else None
            row["status"] = (
                "current"
                if current["requirements_hash"] == metadata["requirements_hash"]
                else "changed"
            )
        except (PixlError, OSError) as error:
            row.update(status="unavailable", reason=str(error))
        result.append(row)
    return result
